### 2026-10-11 – # Oct 9: Wiring up the wings and finding out my LED matrix can't be routed :O

**4.5h**

# Oct 9: Wiring up the wings and finding out my LED matrix can't be routed :O

Alright, so today I finally got both wings wired. Before this, everything was just parts sitting on the butterfly shape with nothing connected.

Now here's the interesting part: the 12x12 RGB LED circle on the right wing can't be routed. I checked the [Harvatek listing](https://www.dasenic.com/product/harvatek-corporation-b36j3rgb-f6c0001hou1930-5631367) and each LED is only 0.65mm. So at a 1mm pitch, that leaves ~0.35mm between them, which fits one thin trace, but every column needs three (R, G, B) plus the row lines crossing them, so I'm switching to 8x8 at 1.5mm pitch, which keeps the same 12mm circle.

Additionally, I also read the [IS31FL3741 datasheet](https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/198/IS31FL3741-1275466.pdf) for the LED driver. It's a 7x7mm QFN-60, way too big and heavy for a wing, so i need to find a smaller driver.

![Routed wings, red is front copper and blue is the back veins](PASTE-IMAGE-LINK-HERE)

still to do: route the 8x8 matrix, and double check the BME688 pin order, since i only assumed it from the BME680.

**Total time spent: [4.5]h**

### 2026-10-11 – # Oct 11: Trying to route the LED matrix (and it did not go well) :(

**8h**

# Oct 11: Trying to route the LED matrix (and it did not go well) :(

Ok so today was mostly me trying to fix the LED matrix and learning why the heck it's harder than it looks.

Last time I found out the 12x12 RGB circle can't be routed at 1mm pitch, so i switched it to 8x8 at 1.5mm pitch and ran my autorouter plugin, and it failed on every row net. I figured the pitch was still too tight, so i tried 6x6 at 2mm pitch, and it failed the exact same way, indicating the pitch wasn't the real problem.

I dug into it and the actual issue is where the driver chip sits. the [IS31FL3741](https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/198/IS31FL3741-1275466.pdf) pins I need (the SW and CS lines) are on the side of the chip that faces away from the matrix. The control lines on the front layer and the ground veins on the back layer make a wall between the matrix and those pins so nothing can get through. The fix is to rotate the driver and move it right under the matrix, which I have not done yet. This also taught me that the LEDs themselves are fine,  the [Harvatek ones](https://www.dasenic.com/product/harvatek-corporation-b36j3rgb-f6c0001hou1930-5631367) are just really small (0.65mm), so every escape route has to be planned.

While that was going on though, i did get a couple of real things done:
- I added two 4.7k pull-up resistors on SDA and SCL on the left wing for the BME688, and rerouted it (still zero clearance violations in my own check)
- Created a BOM straight from the new design, so the counts are real: 112 LEDs (WOW!), 5 small resistors, 2 caps, etc.
- Created an outline of the actual butterfly and rendered it

![ProjectChrysalisOutlineRender](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/CLPSKhbSjITRP3w3PDLTEM4G6qs4wvKw/f8407deca39dda7817fc87fcc9f48c4489f7984ab66d03aad7a1d343b34c21a4.png)

I got a lot to still do, such as move and rotate the driver under the matrix, then try routing again, and find a smaller driver chip since the 7x7mm one is huge for a wing.

**Total time spent: [8]h**
